detail.longDescription: I am trying to compute the diagonal of the Fisher information matrix. I found this code that appears to do just that, but there are some issues with the code. First consider the code in its original form: estimated_fisher = {} for n, p in model.named_parameters(): estimated_fisher[n] = torch.zeros_like(p) model.eval() for i, (input, target) in enumerate(dl, 0): model.zero_grad() output = model(input.to(device)) label = target.to(device) loss = F.nll_loss(F.log_softmax(output, dim=1), label) loss.backward() # populate grad data # accumulate all the gradients for n, p in model.named_parameters(): estimated_fisher[n].data += p.grad.data ** 2 / len(dl) estimated_fisher = {n: p for n, p in estimated_fisher.items()} where dl is a data loader. This produces an error: RuntimeError: only batches of spatial targets supported (3D tensors) but got targets of size: : [32, 1, 420, 420] I can fix this error by changing the code estimated_fisher = {} for n, p in model.named_parameters(): estimated_fisher[n] = torch.zeros_like(p) model.eval() for i, (input, target) in enumerate(dl, 0): model.zero_grad() output = model(input.to(device)) label = target.to(device) loss = F.nll_loss(F.log_softmax(output, dim=1), label[:,0,:,:]) loss.backward() # populate grad data # accumulate all the gradients for n, p in model.named_parameters(): estimated_fisher[n].data += p.grad.data ** 2 / len(dl) estimated_fisher = {n: p for n, p in estimated_fisher.items()} But this results in another error RuntimeError: expected scalar type Long but found Float Again I can modify the code to try and fix this error estimated_fisher = {} for n, p in model.named_parameters(): estimated_fisher[n] = torch.zeros_like(p) model.eval() for i, (input, target) in enumerate(dl, 0): model.zero_grad() output = model(input.to(device)) label = target.to(device) loss = F.nll_loss(F.log_softmax(output, dim=1), label[:,0,:,:].long()) loss.backward() # populate grad data # accumulate all the gradients for n, p in model.named_parameters(): estimated_fisher[n].data += p.grad.data ** 2 / len(dl) estimated_fisher = {n: p for n, p in estimated_fisher.items()} Which results in the error in the title of this post EDIT: On changing my device to cpu I receive the following error message:
